title: Status line: stop false and repeated offers (help text only, a failed folder swap on Windows, a record reset by an old orion)
seam: orion.sh, the status line section, and the status line section of tests/run.sh
story: Computers were asked to take a "new status line" when a release had changed only its help text. On Windows, a failed folder swap left a nested copy that made every later offer say "your own edits", and older orion scripts brought the same question back in a loop. Now the session-start hook and `orion update` stay quiet about help-text-only changes, `statusline merge` replaces the files in place when the folder is busy, and a note in `~/.cache/orion/statusline-seen` keeps what was taken or skipped, so a rewrite by an old orion no longer reopens the question.

checks.criterion: A release that changes only the status line's help text brings no offer, and the computer's copy stays as it is.
checks.steps: In a throw-away HOME, run `orion.sh init --project <tmp-project> --yes --statusline`. Add a sentence to `<tmp-project>/.claude/orion/statusline/README.md`. Raise line 5 of `<tmp-project>/.claude/orion/VERSION` to `2.99.0`. Run `bash .claude/orion/orion.sh check --project <tmp-project>`.

checks.criterion: When the status line folder cannot be renamed, taking orion's status line replaces its files in place.
checks.steps: Start from the state of the help-text check. Add a line to the project's `.claude/orion/statusline/statusline.sh` and raise the version on line 5 of `VERSION`. On Windows, hold `~/.claude/statusline` open (for example, a terminal whose current folder is inside it). Run `bash .claude/orion/orion.sh statusline merge` from the project.
checks.expected: The line "orion's newest taken", the new line in `~/.claude/statusline/statusline.sh`, and no `statusline.new` folder inside the status line folder or beside it.

checks.criterion: A `statusline.new/` folder carrying orion's own `.orion-baseline` is not counted as an edit.
checks.steps: In the throw-away HOME, copy `statusline.sh`, `README.md`, `.orion-base` and `.orion-baseline` from `~/.claude/statusline/` into `~/.claude/statusline/statusline.new/`. Change the project's `.claude/orion/statusline/statusline.sh` and raise the version. Run `bash .claude/orion/orion.sh check --project <tmp-project>`, then `bash .claude/orion/orion.sh statusline merge`.
checks.expected: The check offers with the "Take it" wording, not "Merge them in". After the merge, `~/.claude/statusline/statusline.new/` is gone.

checks.criterion: A record rewritten by an orion from before three-part versions brings no offer while the files are unchanged.
checks.steps: Take a version with `bash .claude/orion/orion.sh statusline merge`. Overwrite `~/.claude/statusline/.orion-baseline` with the two lines `16` and `123 45`. Run `bash .claude/orion/orion.sh check --project <tmp-project>`. Then replace the copy's `statusline.sh` with different content and run the check again.
checks.expected: The first check prints nothing. After the copy's files changed, the check offers the project's status line again.
